facts.fact: CERT-MU published a security bulletin on 22 October 2026 rating the PHP2Shell vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618 and -109619) critical at 9.2, and the government took some state sites offline as a precaution.
The National Cyber Security Committee was immediately seized of the PHP2shell vulnerability, and the government took about 70% of its sites offline on its recommendation, per ICT minister Ramtohul.

The Acting Prime Minister cited figures published by the Mauritius Digital Promotion Agency, based on data from the ICT Authority and CERT-MU, showing reported security incidents rose from 5,221 in 2024 to 6,073 in 2025.

The gazetted regulations refer to the National Cybersecurity Committee established under section 3 of the Cybersecurity and Cybercrime Act 2021, which may designate critical information infrastructure.

note: Regulations set the designation mechanism for five sectors; no system is stated as designated.
CERT-MU is named only as collaborating on a forensic laboratory; no creation, alert or designation is stated; CII audit amendments are planned.

facts.fact: The National Audit Office report, as reported by l'express, says the National Cybersecurity Committee is a body provided for by law and that CERTMU operates under the ministry, though the committee was not operational by end 2025.
The Ministry of ICT's National Cybersecurity Strategy 2023-2026, the successor to the 2014-2019 strategy, sets four pillars; it prints only the year, so as_of is the document's published year.

The strategy states the National Cybersecurity Committee, with 13 members, is the governance body set up under the Cybersecurity and Cybercrime Act 2021 (proclaimed December 2021) to coordinate the strategy and the critical information infrastructure protection framework.
The strategy names CERT-MU as the national CERT, responsible for handling and coordinating incidents of national significance, and records that CERT-MU assisted Zambia's CERT in 2017.
